name: maybe_Battle_ResetCommandQueue
summary: Releases every queued battle-command object of the manager (the intrusive list rooted at +0x110) and clears the 'command queue dirty' byte at +0x13d. Called when a battle action list is rebuilt.
evidence: calls 0x16D854 which walks the +0x110 list and calls vtable+4 on each node; then writes self+0x13d=0. 0x16D854 is only used from command-list teardown paths.

name: Battle_SyncUnitModelTransforms
summary: Walks the four 26-entry battle-unit lists at world+0x428c and copies each live unit's model transform (+0x75c, three words) into the actor/model object registered for that unit id, keeping the rendered monsters and party models on top of their logical battle-unit positions.
evidence: iterates j=0..3, i=0..0x19 over func_002AB62C(world+0x428c+j*0x1c,i); filters on vtable+0x18 (active) and vtable+0xe8(0x5a); unit id at +0x110 is split into group/id and resolved through g_0016bbe8/ec/f0; final call 0x5F5F54(actor, unit+0x75c, 0) writes the 3-word transform and (arg3!=0) orientation. 0x5F5F54 stores those words into +0x120 and derives +0x8c..+0x98.

name: Battle_QueueUnitActions
summary: Collects the actions already chosen by every battle unit (unit field +0xe94) and appends a battle action slot for each one, tagging it with the unit pointer and the manager's action counter before marking the source command as consumed (vtable+0xe4 with 0x5a).
evidence: same 4x26 unit walk as 0x16BA64; for units with piVar2[0x3a5]!=0 it sets local_98=unit, local_48=self->f_11c++ and calls 0x16F28C(self,self->f_124,&entry,g_0016bdac,0,1) (the action-slot insert), then vtable+0xe4(unit,0x5a,1).

name: Battle_BuildTargetList
signature: void Battle_BuildTargetList(BattleManager* self, BattleTarget* out, int count, int* outSideACount, int* outSideBCount)
summary: Builds the candidate-target array for the current action: clears the caller's 8-byte entries, then enumerates the ally list (world+0x4254) and the enemy list (world+0x4270) into one id array. Each output entry receives the target id plus a flag saying whether it came from the first (ally) list.
evidence: initialises count*8 bytes with 0xffffffff/0; 0x2ABAD8(world+0x4254,0,ids,5) returns the first-side count into *arg4, 0x2ABAD8(world+0x4270,*arg4,ids,5) the second into *arg5; 0x2ABAD8 writes ids from entry+0x18 offset by its arg2, proving the concatenation. Loop then stores ids[0] and sets byte +1 = (i < *arg4).

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitCommandPhase
summary: State check for a battle unit's command byte (+0x2f0): recognises the idle/done values plus the three 'ready for input' states, optionally notifies the UI/target subsystem, and finally calls the unit's vtable slot +0x198. Returns 0 for unknown states so the caller can defer the unit.
evidence: reads (char)unit[0xbc]=+0x2f0 and compares it with -1, +0x106, 3, +0x103, +0xfd and +0x40; the accepted branch calls 0x169BC8(unit) and ends in (**(vtable+0x198))(unit). 0x3247DC(world+0x4324,0) is called when world+0x4244 is 1 (in-battle debug/target mode).

name: maybe_Battle_ValidateQueuedCommands
signature: uint32_t maybe_Battle_ValidateQueuedCommands(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Checks whether the queued command objects at world+0x4260 are all valid for the current battle unit: first all entries must pass their vtable+0x10 validation, then each valid entry is offered to the manager's vtable+0x190. Returns 1 when the queue can be executed, 0 otherwise.
evidence: walks the circular list world+0x4260/0x4264, calls (**(vtable+0x10))() on each node, and on the retry pass calls (**(self+0x190))(self,node); returns 0 as soon as one fails. Also consults 0x627B24(self) (battle busy check) before accepting.

name: maybe_Battle_QueueDefaultActions
summary: Fallback command pass: for every active battle unit that has no forced command, appends a default action (id 0x2a) built from the unit's transform/state so the turn can still resolve. Used when AI or player input produced nothing.
evidence: 4x26 unit walk; filters vtable+0x18 !=0, vtable+0x24 !=0, vtable+0x1c==0; builds the same 0x78-byte entry as 0x16BBF4 and calls 0x16F28C(self,self->f_124,entry,0x2a,0,1). Constant 0x2a also appears as a default action id in 0x16D258/0x16DFA8.

name: maybe_Battle_RefreshBattleUi
summary: One-line bridge that fetches the game/world singleton and hands it to 0x207DEC. Looks like a battle-side 'rebuild/refresh HUD or target list' notification; the callee is not recovered as an entry point, so the exact UI element is unconfirmed.
evidence: body is only func_006F1EEC(&stack) followed by func_00207DEC(world). No arguments are used, no globals written locally.

name: maybe_Battle_FinalizeUnitCommands
summary: Second command pass: for each active unit it builds a small action descriptor and, when the unit reports a pending action, calls the unit's vtable+0x50 with 1 (confirm/commit). Complements 0x16C52C which only queues entries.
evidence: 4x26 unit walk; entry+0x18 non-zero; 0x176948/0x1762AC initialise the descriptor with the unit; vtable+0x1c!=0 triggers (**(vtable+0x50))(unit,1). 0x1762AC is also used by 0x174324 for the same unit->descriptor path.

name: Battle_SelectAiActions
summary: Enemy AI turn: for every active battle unit it evaluates the unit's AI table (+0x8f0) against the current battle seed, rolls 1..100, chooses one of the unit's skill/attack ids, applies the skill's target/side rules, and appends the resulting action slots. This is the routine that decides what monsters do each round.
evidence: walks the four 0x1c-stride unit lists and the 0x50 action slots; reads unit->f_770 (remaining AI actions), unit->f_8f0 AI table via 0x2031A4, and skill ids through 0x63FA60/0x63FC70/0x63FD24 (skill data table); random roll func_001CA474(world+0x4218,1,100,0); writes f_e80 AI branch flag; pushes actions with 0x16B810. Skill id constants 0x1df/0x1ea/0x38e/0x548/0x550 are battle skills.

name: maybe_Battle_DispatchUnitAction
signature: void maybe_Battle_DispatchUnitAction(BattleManager* self, BattleUnit* unit, uint32_t actionId, int** outEntry)
summary: Dispatches one battle unit's pending action: reads the unit's action descriptor at +0xb0f7/+0xb0f9 (or the alternate +0xb12a block), looks up the handler in the manager's small function table at self[actionType], runs it, then either appends the entry with 0x16B810 or inserts it with 0x16F28C using action id 0x14.
evidence: reads bytes +0xb0f7/+0xb0f9 on the unit and selects either unit+0xb12a or +0xb14a; indexes self+cVar1*8 (0..10) and calls the two function pointers stored there with (unitId, subId); falls back to 0x16B810(...,0x14,...) or 0x16F28C(...,0x14,0,1). The same +0xb0f7 flag gates 0x16DFA8's choice between 0x16B810 and 0x16F28C.

name: maybe_Battle_SpawnUnitEntryEffects
summary: Counts the battle units that are present and collects their data ids, then hands the lineup descriptor to 0x3FE054, which spawns the per-monster entry/aura effect objects (0x20c-byte effect instances). Runs once when the battle line-up is finalised.
evidence: for each of the 4x26 unit lists it tests vtable+0x18 and self+i*8+200==0, increments self->f_c0 and stores unit->f_768; then fills local_48 from self->f_c4/f_cc..f_e0 and calls 0x3FE054(&self->f_bc,local_48,0). 0x3FE054 allocates 0x20c-byte objects from heap+0x354 and calls 0x20A9B8 with effect ids 0xd..0x80 for each u16 entry.

name: Battle_UpdatePhaseState
summary: Derives the battle phase byte (+0xbc, values 0..8) from a series of virtual predicates on the manager (vtable+0x164..+0x188), so the main battle update can branch on a single state value.
evidence: assigns self->f_bc = 0,1,2,3,5,4,6,7,8 from successive (**(vtable+0x164/0x168/0x16c/0x170/0x174/0x17c/0x180/0x184/0x188))(self) tests, each guarded by the list head check self[0x44]==&self[0x43] and 0x627B24/0x627D04 (battle-busy); world+0x56b4/0x56b8 choose between states 0 and 3.

name: Battle_FreeCommandList
summary: Destroys every node of the manager's queued-command list (+0x110) through the node vtable slot +4. Called when a battle ends or the queue is rebuilt.
evidence: walks self->f_110 circular list; for each node calls (**(code**)(*node+4))(); no other side effects. Callers are 0x16BA4C (queue reset) and 0x16E3E0 (battle teardown), both command-list lifecycle points.

name: Battle_ExecuteItemAction
signature: void Battle_ExecuteItemAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Resolves a battle action that uses an item: reads the item id from the acting unit (vtable+0x84), looks up the item record, hands its id/effect data to the unit, then queues the item-use action (0xf) or its extended variant (0x10). The special item 0x120 (288) with world+0x4e64==0x45 forces a scan of the four unit lists for item 400, i.e. a scripted battle item event.
evidence: 0x61BD4C (Item_LookupRecord) is called with (vtable+0x84)(unit); 0x63DF9C resolves the item data; special case world+0x4e64==0x45, unit+0x768==0 and item==0x120 scans 4 lists at world+0x428c for id 400 with states 0x9e/0x9f; pushes 0xf via 0x16B810 or 0x16F28C, and 0x10 when the scan succeeded.

name: Battle_CountActionTargets
signature: int Battle_CountActionTargets(uint32_t arg1, int arg2, BattleUnit* action)
summary: Counts how many candidates an action may hit: walks the ally container (world+0x4254) and the enemy container (world+0x4270), keeping units whose side matches the action's target mode (vtable+0xa8) and that report targetable (vtable+0x24). Returns the total count.
evidence: two loops over 0x5797D8(world+0x4254/0x4270,0) with 0x2AB62C(index); filters (vtable+0xa8)(action) against 2/3 (side selectors) and (vtable+0x24)(unit) targetable. Sibling 0x16FA10 does the same with vtable+0xac and extra state 10.

name: Battle_Update
summary: Main per-frame battle update: clears finished command objects, runs the queued action processing, executes the AI pass when this frame is not an interrupt, resolves the current action queue, updates the camera/scene hooks, and advances the phase/action counters. Also handles the 'battle over' hand-off to the next state.
evidence: teardown calls 0x16D854/0x16BEDC; then 0x16EB54 (unit action processing), 0x16C7F8 (AI), 0x16B810; 0x171DA4/0x171944/0x1739A0/0x174674 are the scene/camera updates; 0x169ED8/0x16901C finish the frame; resets f_124 (action slot) and f_2f0. Called from the battle state machine in 0x606xxx.

name: maybe_Battle_Start
summary: Virtual battle-start entry: clears the current action slot (-1), initialises the world battle interface, resets the action flags, syncs unit model transforms, notifies the field/weather layer, releases the previous battle scene object (world+0x4320) and finally calls the manager's vtable+0x2c (prepare/finish init).
evidence: starts with func_001BBECC(&self->f_c1) (animation/timer start), self[0x46]=-1, 0x20B49C(world), f_3d=f_3e=0, 0x16BA64 (sync unit transforms), 0x3247B0/0x3247DC on world+0x4324, releases world+0x4320->f_204 through 0x2E0D60, then (**(code**)(*self+0x2c))(self). No direct callers: reached only through the manager vtable.

name: Battle_Initialize
summary: Battle initialisation used when the battle scene is created: same resets as Battle_Start, syncs unit transforms, hides the field view, releases the old battle scene object and calls the manager's vtable+0x2c. Called by the battle-scene setup routine 0x607B7C before its per-slot checks.
evidence: identical body to 0x16E65C minus the 0x1BBECC preamble; single caller 0x607B7C starts with func_0016E680() and then configures the four battle slots (0x3238BC); resets self[0x46], f_3d/f_3e and calls 0x16BA64, 0x3247B0, 0x2E0D60, vtable+0x2c.

name: Battle_UpdateActionQueue
summary: Advances one battle action: asks the manager's virtual predicates whether an action is pending/ready, builds the action queue for the current unit (0x16BBF4) and the default/AI passes, and when the action completes marks the unit list dirty and starts the next action. Returns 0 (the caller keeps ticking).
evidence: calls vtable+0x158/0x15c/0x160/0x18c/0x194/0x1b8/0x1a8 in sequence; when slot+0x2c5 is set calls 0x16BBF4, 0x168AA4, 0x16A78C, 0x16932C (queue building); then 0x16C52C/0x16A3F8 when idle, and 0x16EA5C; f_3d marks 'action list built', f_124 is the slot index.

name: Battle_FindActiveUnit
summary: Scans the manager's command/unit list (world+0x4260) and returns the first unit that is active, not dead and not suppressed, packaged into a small descriptor (0x176948/0x175F80/0x176134). Returns NULL when no unit qualifies. Used to pick 'whose turn is it'.
evidence: iterates world+0x4260..0x4264; checks vtable+0x18 (active), vtable+0x24 (alive), vtable+0x1c (busy), vtable+0xd8 and unit+0x108; calls 0x176948 then 0x175F80(&desc,unit,self->f_148) and 0x176134. 0x175F80 is also used from 0x16E75C for each queued unit.

name: maybe_Battle_ProcessUnitActions
summary: Per-unit action processing for the ally-side container (world+0x4254): for each live, non-suppressed unit it resolves the monster/character data id, then either dispatches the pending action through 0x16D258 or runs the fallback action dispatcher 0x16911C with the unit's category. Decrements the unit's remaining-action counter.
evidence: walks 0x5797D8/0x2AB62C on world+0x4254; filters vtable+0x18/0x20/0x24; id from piVar1[0x1da] (+0x768) resolved by 0x35EB98; special cases data->f_e4==5, byte at g_0016ed30==7, state 0x7d; calls 0x16D258(self,unit) or 0x16911C(self,unit,category,1); decrements piVar1[0x1dc].

name: maybe_Battle_ResolveActionType
signature: void maybe_Battle_ResolveActionType(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Chooses the concrete battle action id for a unit: under the debug/battle flag world+0x4244 it reads the action category from the unit's monster/actor data (+0x31) and maps it to ids 1/2/3/0xe, otherwise uses the normal action id. The action is appended or inserted depending on the unit's +0xb0f7 flag.
evidence: writes a 6-byte descriptor to (vtable+0x58)(unit,&desc) first; reads 0x20D08C(world,unit)->f_31 (action category) and maps 0/1/2/3 to 1/0xe/2/3; calls 0x16B810(self,action,id,...,7) or 0x16F28C(self,self->f_124,action,id,0,1); unit+0xb0f7 selects push vs insert.

name: maybe_Battle_QueueAttackActions
signature: void maybe_Battle_QueueAttackActions(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Queues the two-step attack sequence for a unit: action 0xd (attack/approach) followed by 0x2e (finish). When the unit is in the 'immediate' mode (+0xb0f7) both slots are inserted at the current action index, otherwise appended; flags for the follow-up slot are derived from the unit's alive/state bytes.
evidence: reads unit f_b0f7/f_b0f9/f_10/f_b108; emits 0x16B810(...,0xd,...,uVar3=3 or 7) and (...,0x2e,0,0,8); in the insert path emits 0x16F28C(...,0xd,0,1) then finds the first free action slot (+0x2c5) and inserts 0x2e there. 0x2e/0xd also appear in 0x16FD90/0x1701B0 as follow-up ids.

name: Battle_ResetUnitStates
summary: Clears transient battle state on all units: empties the command list (calling each node's vtable+0x174/0x48 and 0x1CD53C), zeros the per-unit delay fields (+0x8e0/+0x8dc), and resets the four unit-group lists' animation/attack counters. Called between battles or on a full battle reset.
evidence: walks world+0x4260 list calling vtable+0x174(0), +0x48(0), 0x1CD53C(node); zeroes unit+0x8e0/+0x8dc for the 4 units of world+0x4254; for each of the 4 group lists (world+0x428c) calls vtable+0xb8 and zeroes +0x8dc/+0x8e0.

name: Battle_InsertActionSlot
signature: void Battle_InsertActionSlot(BattleManager* self, int index, BattleAction* action, uint32_t actionId, int arg5, uint8_t arg6)
summary: Inserts one 0x2c8-byte action slot at the given index of the manager's 0x50-slot action array: first snapshots every slot into the backup array (+0xec), shifts the range [index..0x4e] up by one, zeroes the new slot, then hands the action descriptor to 0x3CDF74 which fills the slot and its five 0x8c sub-records.
evidence: copies all 0x50 slots from f_e8 to f_ec (5x0x8c each plus the +0x2c0..0x2c6 tail), shifts slots, writes 0xffffffff headers and +0x2c4=6/+0x2c6=1 for the new slot; final call func_003CDF74(f_e8+index*0x2c8+arg5*0x8c, action, 0x2c8, index*0x2c8+700, self, index). Callers use it for action ids 0x14/0x15/1..0x10/0x2a/0x2d/0x2e.

name: Battle_CountActionCandidates
signature: int Battle_CountActionCandidates(uint32_t arg1, int arg2, BattleUnit* action)
summary: Second target-count helper: counts units in the four battle groups plus the ally container that match the action's target mode (vtable+0xac, values 0/1) and are selectable, excluding units with state 10. Used to size/validate target lists.
evidence: 4x26 loop over world+0x428c and a loop over world+0x4254; selects on (vtable+0xac)(action)==0 with (unit vtable+0x18) or ==1 with (unit vtable+0x10); the ally loop additionally requires 0x639954(unit,10)==0. Sibling of 0x16E228 which uses vtable+0xa8/0x24.

name: maybe_Battle_QueueGroupAction
summary: Builds a group action (id 0x2d) for up to four units: prefers units that are active and not already acting, otherwise falls back to any valid unit, then inserts the group action at the current action index. Used for multi-target/combined actions.
evidence: scans world+0x4260 list twice with vtable+0x24/0x18 and (**(self+0x190))(self,unit); stores up to 4 pointers in the local array; if slot 0 is non-NULL calls 0x16F28C(self, self->f_124, list, 0x2d, 0, 1); increments self->f_11c (action counter).

name: Battle_QueueAbilityAction
signature: void Battle_QueueAbilityAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Queues a spell/skill action: reads the ability id (vtable+0x7c), resolves its data through 0x18C184, copies the data flags to the unit, then chooses the action id from the ability's category byte (+0x298: 6,7,8,9,10,0xb) or the default 0x1f/0x20. Also emits the special 0x30/0x31/0x32/0x2e variants for healing/revive/status abilities.
evidence: 0x18C184(abilityId) returns the ability record; (vtable+0x58)(unit, record+0x1f8); record->f_2f3 and first char switch produce 0x30/0x31/0x32/0x2e; record->f_298 switches 0..5 to action ids 7,6,8,9,0xb,10; otherwise 0x1f/0x20. All pushes go through 0x16B810/0x16F28C.

name: maybe_Battle_QueueAbilityActionVariant
signature: void maybe_Battle_QueueAbilityActionVariant(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Sibling of Battle_QueueAbilityAction for the second ability-record table (0x18C1B8): resolves the ability id via vtable+0x78, applies the record to the unit and queues action 4/5 according to the record byte +0xeb, with 0x25/0x26 as fallbacks for invalid records.
evidence: mirrors 0x16FD90 but calls (vtable+0x78)(unit,0) and 0x18C1B8; action ids 4 and 5 are selected by record->f_eb (0/1); invalid record falls back to 0x25/0x26; the unit's +0xb0f7 flag again selects append (0x16B810) vs insert (0x16F28C).

name: Battle_ResetLineupState
summary: Resets the battle line-up bookkeeping (counters f_c0/f_c4/f_cc/f_d0/f_d4/f_d8/f_dc/f_e0 to 0xffff/0, flags f_f2/f_129, f_148) and then calls 0x16D438 to (re)spawn the unit entry effects. Used when the battle line-up changes or a battle is initialised.
evidence: writes self->f_f2=1, f_148=0, f_fc/f_c4/f_d0/f_cc/f_d8/f_d4/f_e0/f_dc/f_c0/f_129 then calls 0x16D438(self) (the effect-spawn pass over the unit lists) and stores g_00170410 in self+0x130.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionScene
summary: Advances the presentation of the current battle action: tracks a state value at +0x134 (waiting on a unit animation/effect), creates the hit/impact effect through 0x3FE054 and 0x35FF3C at the acting unit's position, selects the model/effect by unit id (0x63E5C8/0x633C38/0x633DCC), and updates the camera/scene target. Returns 1 while the action still needs frames.
evidence: state at self+0x134 compared with g_001709a4/g_001709a4+0x34/+0x38/-1; tests float at self->f_e4+8 against 1.5f and g_001709d8; calls 0x3FE054(&self->f_bc,desc,1) to spawn effects; 0x63E5C8/0x633C38/0x633DCC resolve model+animation by unit id; 0x35FF3C creates the effect at g_001709d0; self->f_13d gates the effect and sets f_134 on completion.

name: maybe_Battle_CheckUnitsCondition
signature: int maybe_Battle_CheckUnitsCondition(BattleManager* self, uint32_t mode, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Boolean battle-condition query used by the state machine: mode 4 compares arg3<=arg4, mode 5 asks the world for a value (0x206BA4), mode 6 requires every group unit to pass 0x1CABF4, mode 7 requires every unit to have state 0x33, mode 8 returns world+0x4252. Used to decide when all units have finished an animation/command.
evidence: switch(arg2) 4..8; case 6/7 walk the 4 group lists at world+0x428c and test 0x1CABF4(unit)/0x1CB738(unit,0x33); case 8 reads the byte world+0x4252; callers 0x1745E8 pass the four stored command ids and 0x174324 uses the result for its next state.

name: maybe_Battle_QueueUnitListAction
signature: void maybe_Battle_QueueUnitListAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleUnit** out)
summary: Collects up to eight active, targetable battle units into the caller's array and queues action 0x2f (a group/area action) with the acting unit as source. Similar to 0x16FBF8 but without the 'prefer idle units' pass.
evidence: walks world+0x4260 list keeping units with vtable+0x24, vtable+0x18, vtable+0xd8==0 and no states 8/10 (0x639954), max 8 entries; then 0x16815C computes the source unit value and 0x16B810(self,out,0x2f,value,0,0) queues the action.

name: Battle_SelectActionTargets
signature: int Battle_SelectActionTargets(BattleManager* self, BattleUnit** out, int groupIndex, uint32_t arg4, uint32_t arg5)
summary: Chooses the concrete target(s) of an action: dispatches on the action's target-mode virtual +0xa4 (single, one group, all, self, random) and range checks via +0xb0, then fills out[8..] with the selected unit pointers and returns the count. This is the routine behind every 'who gets hit' decision.
evidence: first calls (vtable+0xa4)(action) and switches modes 3/4/5: mode 3 collects all units from the four group lists (world+0x428c) plus allies (world+0x4254); mode 4 returns the acting unit; mode 5 picks one ally or, for groupIndex<0, all allies; modes 1/2 delegate to 0x16E228/0x16FA10; +0xb0(x,y) calls are the shape/range validity checks.

name: maybe_Battle_SelectGroupTargets
signature: uint32_t maybe_Battle_SelectGroupTargets(BattleManager* self, BattleAction* action, BattleUnit* source, int groupIndex)
summary: Target selection for group/row actions: counts the units of group `groupIndex` matching the action's target mode, and when the action record has the 'group' flag (g_001714d0) marks the group's leader as the primary target (action+0x20). Falls back to counting all groups when no primary target was set.
evidence: walks world+0x428c+groupIndex*0x1c, selects by (action vtable+0xac)==0 -> unit vtable+0x18 or ==1 -> unit vtable+0x10; if byte g_001714d0[action]!=0 calls 0x627800(self,action,leader) and sets action->f_20; otherwise repeats the count over all four groups.

name: maybe_Battle_FinishBattleScene
summary: Shuts down the battle presentation layer: tells the battle scene object (world+0x4320->f_204) to hide/animate out, spawns its closing popup through 0x2DFDE8, invokes the scene object's vtable+0x2c, and releases the battle effect manager at world+0x431c.
evidence: fetches world+0x4320 (battle scene); calls (**(scene->f_204+0x18))(obj,1) and (+0x74)(obj,0); 0x2DFDE8(obj,g_001715bc,...); then (**(scene vtable+0x2c))(); finally 0x269B24(world+0x431c).

name: maybe_Battle_CloseBattleScene
summary: Second half of the battle-scene teardown: calls the scene object's vtable+0x28 (close) and releases the battle effect manager at world+0x431c. Shorter sibling of 0x1714D4, used when no popup is needed.
evidence: world+0x4320->f_204 vtable+0x28() then 0x2695DC(world+0x431c); no arguments used and no state written.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionAnim
summary: Advances the per-action animation pair at self+0x304/+0x35c (0x4B8A84 interpolates them) and, when the battle scene is still active, sets the current actor (self->f_e4) to state 8 (animation done). Always returns 1 so the state machine continues.
evidence: calls 0x4B8A84(&self->f_35c,&self->f_304); if world+0x4320!=0 and 0x640348(scene)!=0 calls (**(self->f_e4+0x14))(self->f_e4,8); returns 1 unconditionally.

name: maybe_Battle_CheckActionAnimEnd

summary: Plays the animation for an NPC action: if the actor has a gesture/action track (f_58/f_11c) and the named action exists (0x641628), uses primaryId, otherwise falls back to fallbackId. Both paths call the actor's vtable+0x84.
evidence: reads actor[0x58]->f_11c and 0x641628(track); if found -> (**(vtable+0x84))(actor,arg2) else (**(vtable+0x84))(actor,arg3). Called from 0x1775D4 with the two registered action tables g_00177608/g_00177604.

name: maybe_Field_NpcPlayLinkedAnimation
signature: void maybe_Field_NpcPlayLinkedAnimation(NpcBehavior* self, uint8_t animId, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Applies an animation to the current NPC action slot's linked animation object through 0x28CDE0 (with the NPC as owner), used for actions that drive a child/partner actor as well.
evidence: same table index as 0x17A2D8 but without the extra stride constant (g_0017a8a8); takes record->f_10 and calls 0x28CDE0(anim,self,animId).

name: Field_NpcApplyAction
summary: Applies a parsed NPC action record: copies its 16 words (speed, animation, move flags, object ids) into the NPC object, resolves the animation object (0x2D71AC) and the action record for the current table (0x62D5DC/0x62D65C), and for flag 1 spawns the 'moveSt' action; for the paired record it spawns 'movePa'. Flag 0x40 ends the action.
evidence: copies rec->f_c..f_4c into self[0x9a..0xaa]; 0x2D71AC(rec->f_14) -> self[0xac], self[0xab]=+f_18*10; self[0xad]=0x62D5DC/0x62D65C(levelMgr,rec->f_1c,rec->f_10); if rec->f_4e&1 -> 0x2A8874(actor,3), allocate 0x34 bytes and 0x2B2F40(...,"moveSt"); if the slot record 0x62B8A4 fails -> allocate 0x44 bytes and 0x2B2ED0(...,"movePa"); if rec->f_4e&0x40 -> (vtable+0x40)(self,4), (vtable+0xb4)(self,2,1).

name: maybe_Field_NpcFinishAction
signature: void maybe_Field_NpcFinishAction(NpcBehavior* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Ends the current NPC action: if the action slot is valid it sends animation id 3 through 0x28CDE0, then lets the actor/sprite system finish the action (0x336938) so the NPC returns to its idle behaviour.
evidence: guards self->f_41; indexes the action table with g_0017ac98/g_0017ac9c and calls 0x28CDE0(anim,self,3); finally 0x336938(self) (same finish helper as 0x17AEE4).

name: maybe_Field_NpcActionDestroy
summary: Destructor tail for the NPC action object: releases the two actor handles at +0x260/+0x264 via 0x336B3C and frees the object block (0x10F6CC).
evidence: reads arg1[0x98]/arg1[0x99] (offsets 0x260/0x264), calls 0x336B3C (sprite/actor release, also used by 0x17ABF8) then 0x10F6CC (free).

name: maybe_Ui_GetTableEntry
summary: Lazily initialises the global 8-byte-record table g_0017bafc (0x10009C constructor) and returns the entry for the given index. Tiny table accessor used by the fade-window code.
evidence: if ((*g_0017baf8 & 1)==0) 0x10009C(g_0017baf8); return g_0017bafc + index*8. No other state; the table base is a data symbol, not a function.

name: Ui_FadeWindow_Setup
summary: Builds the full-screen fade overlay: loads the 'win_fade' layout into the widget at self+0x138 (0x1D85EC) and starts its open animation (0x29126C with 1).
evidence: passes the literal string "win_fade" to 0x1D85EC(self, self+0x138, "win_fade", 0), then 0x29126C(self+0x138,1). 0x1D85EC is the same layout-loader used by other window setup paths.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateFadeWindow
summary: Constructor for the fade overlay object: allocates the base object (0x1D8B6C), initialises its intro/outro child lists and colour-transform block (0x1A66A0), installs the fade vtables (g_0017bf98/9c) and stores the caller's screen mode in +0x128. Returns the object.
evidence: calls 0x1D8B6C (UI object allocator), writes vtable words g_0017bf98/g_0017bf9c, builds two intrusive list heads at +0x120/+0x128 (self-referencing), 0x1A66A0(self+0x138) for the transform, copies g_0017bff0.. colour words, stores arg2 at +0x128; returns self+0 (puVar4-0x4e). 0x17BFB4 is the matching destructor.

name: Ui_FadeWindow_Destroy
summary: Destructor for the fade overlay created by Ui_CreateFadeWindow: releases the embedded transform/widget (0x291220, 0x1A6768), runs the layout destructor (0x1D8C2C at -0x138) and frees the block (0x10F6CC).
evidence: calls 0x291220(self+0x4e), 0x1A6768(self+0x4e), 0x1D8C2C(self+0x4e-0x138), 0x10F6CC; object offsets match 0x17BE9C exactly.

name: maybe_Ui_RegisterActor
signature: uint32_t maybe_Ui_RegisterActor(UiActorHolder* holder, UiActor* actor, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Registers a UI/sprite actor with the holder object and notifies the sprite manager: stores the actor's packed id pair in +0xc/+0xd, bumps the reference count, calls 0x339FC0(world+0x58, holder) to link/visibility-toggle it, and decrements the remaining-life counter.
evidence: checks (holder vtable+0xc)(); writes arg2->f_4 into +0xc and arg3->f_4 into +0xd, +0xe=0xfffffff, +0x10++; calls 0x339FC0(world+0x58,holder) which sets param_1+0x14=param_2 and calls 0x1A1774(...,2,1/0); decrements +0xf. Called from 0x180B94/0x1835AC/0x184958 to register table actors.

name: maybe_Ui_RegisterActorVariant
signature: uint32_t maybe_Ui_RegisterActorVariant(UiActorHolder* holder, UiActor* actor, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)

name: maybe_Ui_ObjectDestroyThunk

name: maybe_Ui_SetupWidgetAnimation
summary: Binds a UI animation to the widget: fetches the animation track (0x2BBF6C), resolves the named animation data (0x62AB3C) and installs it with 0x1A6210 under the widget's vtable+0x34 animation slot, using g_0017c894 as the descriptor.
evidence: calls 0x2BBF6C (anim track), 0x62AB3C (named anim lookup), (**(vtable+0x34))(widget,&g_0017c894,*(u16*)(widget+0x28)<<16,0) and 0x1A6210(widget, id<<16, animData); fallback branch builds an animation via g_0017c89c/0x627308 and 0x633560(...,0xfb).

name: maybe_Ui_ObjectDestroyThunk2

name: maybe_Ui_CreateMapCursor
summary: Creates the map cursor/marker instance: resolves the marker definition for self->f_e0, allocates a 0x280-byte actor (0x1CE8AC) from the world's UI heap and registers it with 0x21F738, then activates it through vtable+0x24.

name: maybe_Ui_DestroyMapCursor

name: maybe_Ui_SetupWindowAnimations
summary: Loads the window's two idle animations ('anim01' and 'anim_01') into +0x120 and +0x124, binding the first from the widget's animation list (0x53649C) and the second from its timeline (0x3E00CC).
evidence: literal strings "anim01" and "anim_01"; calls 0x53649C(self->f_ac,"anim01") -> self->f_120 and 0x3E00CC(&self->f_124,self->f_98,"anim_01",0).

name: Ui_WorldMap_UpdateShipIcon
signature: void Ui_WorldMap_UpdateShipIcon(UiWorldMap* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3)
summary: Places the ship/vehicle icon on the world map: reads the current map node and its per-map offset/scale tables from the world-map data (0x66B7C0/0x66B724/0x66B5D8/0x66B738/0x66B91C) and forwards the resulting 2D point to Ui_MapShipIcon_Update (0x3A7C4C). Also applies the map's rotation offset to the five marker objects.
evidence: reads world+0x24a98 world-map object via 0x66B7C0/0x66B738, indexes the node tables at mapObj->f_60 and f_78, then calls func_003A7C4C (named Ui_MapShipIcon_Update in N_010) with the computed point; five marker objects at self+0x48..+0x58 are updated with the rotated offsets g_0017d7f0. Strings none, but every callee is a world-map data accessor.

name: Ui_SelectPage
summary: Selects one of the five page actors of a pager widget: highlights the matching actor (0x292B48(actor, i==page)), copies its transform into +0x98..+0xa4, stores the page index in +0xa8 and notifies the parent through 0x621358/0x628464.
evidence: reads the page byte *(u8*)(self+arg2+0x24); loops i<5 over self+0x48+i*4 calling 0x292B48(actor,i==page); 0x291678(&self->f_98) then stores the 4 words; self->f_a8=arg2; 0x628464(self)->0x621358(self->f_20,value). Also used as a UI pager/status screen selector.

name: maybe_Ui_ReleasePageActors
summary: Releases the five page actors of the pager (calls 0x2914D4 on each non-null actor at self+0x48).
evidence: loop i<5: if *(int*)(arg1+i*4+0x48)!=0 call 0x2914D4(); no other side effects.

name: maybe_Ui_UpdatePageSelection
signature: void maybe_Ui_UpdatePageSelection(UiPager* self, uint32_t arg2, int arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Applies a page selection change on the pager and mirrors it into the party-status screen: looks up the selected page actor, enables the party status display (0x23C72C(world+0x48,1,0)) and updates the pager state (0x62155C).
evidence: reads self->f_a8 and the page byte; if the selected actor exists, 0x23C72C(world+0x48,1,0) (named Party_Status_SetEnabled) and 0x62155C(self); the alternate branch calls 0x17FC64(self,...).

name: maybe_Ui_ApplyPageHighlight
summary: Sets the pointer/hover highlight on the pager's five page actors: gives the current page actor the highlight flag (f_9f4=1), clears it on the other four, and updates the parent window's cursor state.
evidence: if self->f_91==0: sets f_60->f_9f4=1 and clears f_48/f_4c/f_50/f_54/f_58->f_9f4; then 0x621550/0x6215FC on self->f_20 or f_20->f_94=0.

name: maybe_Ui_ResetPageFlag
summary: Clears the pager's busy flag (+0x2a3) when the world UI query 0x636AFC returns false.
evidence: if 0x636AFC(world+0x6c)==0 then self->f_2a3=0. Nothing else.

name: maybe_Field_CreateEffectSprite
signature: void maybe_Field_CreateEffectSprite(FieldObject* self, int* arg2, int* arg3)
summary: Creates a positioned sprite/effect on a field object: merges the two caller point arrays (0x47B280/0x47B460) into a transform, then attaches a sprite child (0x335A6C) using the world's 2D mode (world+0x48->f_27f) and stores its handle in +0x29c.
evidence: builds local_98 descriptor from g_00180578, reads the world 2D mode byte world+0x48->0x27f, 0x47B280/0x47B460 (point/rect merge), then 0x335A6C(self,&desc,&self->f_254,0); result stored in self->f_29c (0xff on failure). 0x335A6C is maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild from N_022.

name: Field_CreateCollisionSprite
summary: Creates the field object's collision proxy: builds the rectangle from the caller's point list, allocates a 0x68-byte sprite (0x4C65A0) and a 0xa4-byte collision object named 'collision' (0x4C3B50), then registers both through 0x5F4F34/0x5F4E94.
evidence: literal string "collision"; allocates 0x68 bytes and 0xa4 bytes from self->f_48, 0x4C65A0/0x4C3B50 create the objects, 0x5F4F34/0x5F4E94 store them on self; the world 2D mode byte world+0x48->0x27f chooses the collision depth flags f_4c/f_50/f_58.

name: maybe_Field_UpdateObjectHandle
summary: Forwards an update to the sprite/effect handle stored in the page array at +0x204 (index +0x29c) through 0x3DF8D8; clears the busy flag if the update rejected it.
evidence: if self->f_29c != 0xff and self[+0x204+index*4]!=0, sets f_2a3=1, calls 0x3DF8D8(obj+0x3c,arg2,g_0018090c), and clears f_2a3 when it returns 0.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyTransform
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyTransform(FieldSceneObject* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Applies a scene object's size/position: sets the model size (Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize 0x5F3500), refreshes the object handle (0x5F36E0), resolves the object's actor record by id (0x1C8F58), stores it in +0x22c and updates the actor's movement state (0x5E7848).
evidence: calls 0x5F4034, 0x5F3500(self,self->f_240,self->f_242), 0x5F36E0(self,self->f_244,1), 0x1C8F58(world+0x54,f_36,0) then resolves the object type and stores self->f_22c; self->f_246=(0x62AB3C(world)!=0); 0x5E7848(self,2 or 0,1).

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Refresh
summary: Lightweight refresh of a scene object: updates its animation (0x5E780C) and re-applies the actor movement state derived from +0x246.
evidence: 0x5E780C(self); state = f_246?2:0; 0x5E7848(self,state,1); if it returns non-zero and f_29f/f_b8 are set calls 0x460274().

name: maybe_Field_RegisterAnimActors
summary: Creates actors for new entries of the field object's animation table (self->f_248): walks the entries after the last processed index (+0x2ac), resolves each entry's object (0x33D99C) and registers it with 0x17C054.
evidence: requires world->f_44==0 and self->f_248!=0; loops i=f_2ac+1..f_2b0, skips entries with count<=0, resolves 0x33D99C(world+0x58, entry) and calls 0x17C054(obj,self,0); stores f_2ac=f_2b0.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_TriggerEffect
signature: int maybe_Field_Gadget_TriggerEffect(FieldObject* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Triggers a field gadget command: allocates the command/effect object (0x1EBC68) and issues gadget command 10 with the object's id (+4) through 0x256678. Clears the busy flag on failure.
evidence: allocates via g_001811a4 pool and 0x1EBC68(block,9,0,0); calls 0x256678(world+0x6c,10,self->f_4) (named Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand in N_022); on 0 sets self->f_2a3=0, else triggers 0x460274.

name: maybe_Ui_DestroySubObject
summary: Destructor helper: runs the small-object destructor on the embedded object at self+0x254, releases its sprite (0x335DAC) and frees the block.
evidence: 0x17C334(self+0x95*4) -> obj, then 0x335DAC(obj-0x254), 0x10F6CC(). 0x181330 is the same without the free.

name: maybe_Ui_DestroySubObjectNoFree
summary: Same as 0x18130C but does not free the outer block (used when the object is embedded in a larger allocation).
evidence: 0x17C334(self+0x254) then 0x335DAC(obj-0x254); no 0x10F6CC call.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Register
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_Register(FieldSceneObject* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Registers the scene object's current transform with the field renderer when it is visible and has a model: sets +0x264, and calls 0x5F58D0(self, world+0x54->f_1c->f_4) once, then clears the pending flag +0x265.
evidence: sets f_264=1; checks f_15c/f_15d/f_310/f_265; reads world+0x54->f_1c (the field camera/scene object), uses its +4 word (or g_001817bc), calls 0x5F58D0(self,value) and f_265=0.

name: maybe_Field_CheckObjectState
signature: bool maybe_Field_CheckObjectState(FieldObject* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Checks a world/field state flag (0x636AFC) and, when it is clear, calls the object's vtable+0xc4; returns whether the flag was set.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Release
summary: Releases a field scene object's attached effect and actor resources: destroys the effect at +0x384 (0x3F422C->vtable+0x88), releases the attached object (0x5F58BC) and clears the party/window reference.
evidence: if *(int*)(arg1+900)!=-1 resolves 0x5F708C and calls 0x225BF4; 0x3F422C(self->f_370) -> vtable+0x88; then 0x5F58BC(self). Same helpers as 0x181C14.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_UpdateShadow
summary: Updates the scene object's shadow/billboard: resolves the shadow definition for the object id (+0x258), places it with 0x17CB7C and copies the resulting size/offset into the actor's shadow fields (+0x364..+0x36c), then shifts the child shadows by the height delta.
evidence: allocates via 0x627308 pool, 0x5EB3A0 builds the query, 0x6282D0/0x6368EC resolve the object, 0x17CB7C(manager,0,def,&pos,&offset,query) places it; loops self->f_250 children at self+0x230 setting f_304..f_318.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_UpdateVisibility
summary: Visibility/animation update for a field scene object: if the attached effect exists and is not hidden, calls its vtable+0x84 with the new value, then lets the actor system apply it (0x5F6000).
evidence: if *(int*)(arg1+900)!=-1 -> 0x5F708C/0x225BF4; 0x3F422C(self->f_370) and if *(char*)(obj+0x51)==0 calls (**(vtable+0x84))(obj,arg2); then 0x5F6000(self,arg2).

name: maybe_Field_Actor_CreateSprite
signature: void maybe_Field_Actor_CreateSprite(FieldActor* self, uint32_t arg2, int arg3)
summary: Creates the actor's billboard/sprite representation: picks the sprite definition for the actor's type (0x66A74C/0x628EE0/0x63EE68), allocates a 0x70-byte sprite through 0x4C6B28, attaches it with 0x5F7E60, and optionally creates the collision proxy named 'collision' (0x4C3E38).
evidence: builds a sprite descriptor from g_00182118.. and the actor id f_36, uses 0x66A74C/0x628EE0; special ids 0x219..0x21c tweak the colour/scale; allocates 0x70 bytes, 0x4C6B28(block,&desc,&ctx,self), 0x5F7E60(self,sprite); if f_350!=0 allocates 0x6c bytes and 0x4C3E38(...,"collision") with g_00182154.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateModel
summary: Per-frame model update for a field actor: resolves its object handle by type (0x1C8EDC), applies ground/effect offsets (0x30A0E0/0x30AC50), drives the model's animation/transform (0x6289CC/0x223C84/0x1D5C94) and updates the actor's collision position (0x2E7F08).
evidence: 0x5E7598 first; 0x1C8EDC(world+0x54,f_36,0) -> self[0x98]; if f_2c4? calls 0x30A0E0; vtable+0xd0; switches on model->f_120 (0xdc/0xdd/0xab etc.) to offset the model; 0x6289CC, 0x223C84(model,&offset), 0x30AC50, 0x1D5C94(model+0x52c); 0x2E7F08 for the collision position.

name: Model_Equip_UpdateActorEquipment
summary: Refreshes the actor's visible equipment: resolves the model set (0x1C7EA4 / 0x35EB98), updates both equipment rows through 0x40BA94/0x4062F0-style calls, then applies the accessory slots (Model_Equip_ApplyAccessorySlots 0x40AE18), grip state (0x40B748) and final model refresh (0x40AC10).
evidence: 0x1C7EA4(self->f_36) -> f_e5; 0x40BA94(model,type); for each of two rows resolves 0x6292F0/0x640068 and calls (**(model vtable+8))(&self->f_e3,&row,0); then 0x40BA78, 0x40B748(model,0,1), 0x40AE18(model,1,model->f_68), 0x40AC10. Explicit Model_Equip_* callees from N_022.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_PlayIdleAnimation
summary: Plays the actor's idle/extra animation selected by its type (+0x313) via 0x5F7948, falling back to the default animation, and adjusts the actor's size (+0x374) through 0x5F7784 when a height mismatch is detected.
evidence: 0x5F7948(self,g_00182ac0[f_313]) then fallback 0x5F7948(self,*g_00182ac0); if f_374>=0 calls 0x66A244(self), compares the converted height and calls 0x5F7784(self,delta,0); clears f_160->f_555/f_550/f_556.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition
summary: Computes the field camera's follow position: if a rail/route table is attached (+0x314) it takes the current route point's position and rotation, otherwise it searches up to ten candidate positions along the target direction (using the level collision query 0x2E7F08) and stores the first clear spot in +0x328..+0x330.
evidence: when f_314==0: uses target f_318 (position f_c/f_10, radius f_18/f_28, angle f_30), 0x51B1FC random, 0x6731EC/0x672E44 sin/cos, 0x574548 rotate, 0x2E7F08 collision test, stores f_328/f_32c/f_330; else reads route entry f_314[f_340] (0x28 bytes) and 0x572D94/0x574548 for the rotation, stores f_334..f_33c. f_324 selects forward/backward.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_CreateBillboard
summary: Creates the actor's floating billboard/marker (name plate, quest icon or damage text): fills the 0x224-byte billboard descriptor with colour/scale/font fields, allocates it through 0x3F4510, registers it with the actor (0x1235A4) and stores the handle in +0x370. Also rebuilds the billboard's rotation matrix.
evidence: 0x3F42B0(&local_80,arg2) prepares the descriptor (many immediates 0x78/200/0x10), 0x109DC8(0x224,self->f_48,4), 0x3F4510(block,&desc), then vtable+0xc(desc), 0x1235A4(world+0x140,...,obj) registers; self->f_370=obj[1]; 0x3F422C() then 0x5F56A0(...) updates the matrix. 0x3F422C/0x3F42B0 are the billboard/2D-sprite APIs.

name: maybe_Field_UpdateCullingFlag
summary: Distance culling: when the actor is not hidden, compares its distance to the player with g_00183568 (and its own +0x25c threshold) and sets/clears bit 1 of the culling flags (+0x50) so the renderer can skip far actors.
evidence: if f_219==0 calls 0x5F7888; if world->f_44==0 and f_50==0 and g_00183568<=f_25c: 0x63451C gives the player position, computes squared distance including the f_25c term, sets f_50 |= 2 or &= 0xfd.

name: maybe_Field_RegisterRailActors
summary: Creates actors for the entries of the actor's rail/animation table (+0x314) that became active since the last frame: resolves each entry with 0x33D99C and registers it via 0x17C054.
evidence: same structure as 0x180B94 but the table is self->f_314 with 0x28-byte entries and indices f_354..f_358; requires world->f_44==0.

name: maybe_Field_SpawnObjectRecordA

name: Script_ParseAssignmentExpression
signature: void Script_ParseAssignmentExpression(ScriptCompiler* comp, uint32_t* lhs, uint32_t mode)
summary: Assignment/ternary expression parser of the Squirrel compiler: handles '=' (0x3d) and '?' (0x3f) including the short-jump fixups for the ternary branches, brackets/parentheses around the value, and emits the assignment opcode plus line-info records. Recurses into itself for nested assignments.
evidence: token comparisons against '=' 0x3d, '?' 0x3f, '[' 0x5b, ')' 0x28, '.' 0x2e and keywords 0x119/0x121/0x12f/0x130/0x13d..0x13f; calls func_005FC86C (the lexer) and func_001BDD50 to emit opcodes (0x1a/0x18/0x21/0x2c/0xe); uses func_001BE454/0x1BCE5C/0x1BE384 for line/column fixups. Called by 0x186150 (postfix parser) for index/call arguments.

name: Script_ParseBitwiseExpression
summary: Bitwise operator parser: loops over '&' (0x26), '^' (0x5e) and '|' (0x7c), calls the next-level expression parser through the compiler's operator table (comp->f_18/f_10/f_8) and emits the bitwise opcode (0x12 with sub-op 0/3/2).
evidence: three while loops comparing *arg1 against 0x26, 0x5e, 0x7c; calls (*comp->f_18/f_10/f_8) with the operator index and emits opcode 0x12 plus sub-op 0,3,2 via 0x1BDD50; obtains line/column with 0x1BE454/0x1BCE5C. Squirrel compiler uses exactly this operator-table indirection.

name: Script_ParseUnaryExpression
summary: Unary prefix parser: while the current token is 0x10f (unary operator, e.g. '-'/'!'/'~'/'++'), parses the operand recursively, emits the unary opcode (0x2c) and patches the line info; otherwise falls through to the binary expression parser (0x186B28).
evidence: if (*arg1 == 0x10f) { emit opcode 0x2c; lexer 0x5FC86C; recurse func_00186020; } else func_00186B28; line fixups via 0x1BE454/0x1BE384. 0x10f is the unary-operator keyword id used by the same compiler.

name: Script_ParsePostfixExpression
summary: Postfix expression parser: handles member access '.' (0x2e), indexing '[' ... ']' (0x5b/0x5d) and calls '(' ... ')' (0x28/0x29). For calls it counts the arguments (opcode 6 with the arg count), for indexing it emits the index opcode (0x21/0x1/0xe), and for member access it resolves the field name through the compiler table. Also inserts line-break records when a newline appears inside brackets.
evidence: handles tokens 0x5b '[' / 0x5d ']' / 0x2e '.' / 0x28 '(' / 0x29 ')' and 0x2c ','; emits opcode 6 with the argument count via 0x1BDD50; 0x185720 is called for the index/argument expressions; 0x1874EC consumes the closing tokens; 0x187780 starts the parse; line markers g_001868e8/ec/f0/f4/f8/fc.

name: maybe_Script_ParseBitwiseAnd
summary: Lowest-level bitwise-and parser: while the token is '&' (0x26) it calls the operand parser through the compiler table (comp->f_18) and emits the bitwise opcode (0x12). Sub-parser of the 0x186B28/0x1869C4 chain.
evidence: single while loop on *arg1==0x26 calling (*comp->f_18)() and emitting opcode 0x12 via 0x1BDD50; identical body shape to the first loop of 0x185E18, which is the combined bitwise parser.

name: maybe_Script_ParseBitwiseXor
summary: Bitwise-xor level parser: loops on '&' then '^' (0x26/0x5e), calling the operand parser and emitting opcode 0x12 with sub-op 3 for xor. Sits between 0x185E18 and 0x186904 in the operator chain.
evidence: two while loops on 0x26 and 0x5e, both calling the compiler operator table (f_18/f_10) and emitting 0x12 with sub-ops 0/3 via 0x1BDD50; no other side effects.

name: maybe_Script_ParseBinaryExpression
summary: Middle-level binary expression parser: parses a bitwise expression (0x185E18), then loops on the comparison/equality keyword tokens 0x10e, 0x118 and 0x137, emitting the corresponding jump/patch opcodes (0x2b/0x2a) and delegating to 0x1889EC for the two-operand forms. Recurses for the right-hand side.
evidence: starts with 0x185E18; while(*arg1==0x10e) emits opcode 0x2b and recurses 0x186B28; for 0x118 -> 0x1889EC(comp,0x29,...), for 0x137 -> 0x1889EC(comp,0x2a,...); line fixups 0x1BE454/0x1BE384. Called by 0x186020 (unary) and 0x185720 (assignment).

name: maybe_Script_ParseStatementList
signature: void maybe_Script_ParseStatementList(ScriptCompiler* comp, uint32_t separator, uint32_t terminator)
summary: Statement-list/block parser of the Squirrel compiler: parses statements until the terminator token, accepting ';' (0x3b) or ',' as separators, and handles leading '[' (0x5b), keyword tokens 0x140/0x142, 0x11d/0x136 and the function/closure forms. Also inserts a line record after every parsed statement (0x3c opcode).
evidence: while (*comp != terminator): if separator==0x3b handles [ / 0x140/0x142; for 0x11d/0x136 calls 0x1BD318 & 0x1BD000, emits opcode 0x3c; calls 0x1874EC, 0x185720, 0x186CB4, 0x189228; 0x1BE384 patches the statement extent. This is the top-level statement dispatcher used by 0x185720/0x186150.
